causes.text: In late August 2024, Temu owner PDD Holdings suffered its biggest one-day share price tumble since 2018, wiping out nearly $55 billion in market capitalisation. Executives warned that stiff competition and increased investments would hurt revenue growth.

source_info.title: China's PDD suffers $55 bln market cap wipeout after flagging an uncertain market

causes.text: On July 2 2025, Alibaba Group announced a 50 billion yuan (US$7 billion) subsidy initiative aimed at its instant commerce operations. The programme offered discounts, cash rewards and red envelopes to consumers and merchants, reflecting its plan to refocus on core commerce amid intensifying competition.

source_info.title: Alibaba Offers $7 Billion of Subsidies to Defend Turf in China

effects.text: By mid-August 2025, JD.com reported that its adjusted operating margin had shrunk to 0.3% from 4% a year earlier. Analysts said an escalating subsidy war-sparked by rivals' heavy spending and intensified by PDD's earlier market turmoil-forced JD.com to match promotions, which eroded profitability.

source_info.title: JD.com faces battle to gain ground in China's instant delivery market

causal_reasoning_chain.description: PDD's stock crash signaled that investors were nervous about profitability in the low-margin instant-commerce market. Executives warned that competition and rising investment would hurt revenue growth, hinting at a more aggressive subsidy environment.

Less than a year later, Alibaba launched a massive 50 billion yuan subsidy programme to defend its turf in instant commerce. The move aimed to stimulate consumption but effectively raised the stakes by giving consumers steep discounts and cash rewards.

JD.com, already investing heavily in rapid-delivery services, faced pressure to match competitors' giveaways to avoid losing market share. The confluence of PDD's earlier cautionary signals and Alibaba's aggressive subsidies created a highly competitive environment that forced JD.com to cut prices and increase spending.

The escalating subsidy war eroded JD.com's profitability. By August 2025 the company reported its adjusted operating margin had plunged to 0.3%, and its stock slid roughly 4% as investors digested the cost of staying competitive.

rationale: PDD's share-price wipeout highlighted the financial risks of competing in the instant-commerce space. When Alibaba subsequently rolled out a massive subsidy plan, JD.com had little choice but to follow suit. These combined pressures triggered a subsidy war that undermined JD.com's margins.
counterfactual_analysis: If PDD had not telegraphed weakness and Alibaba had refrained from its generous subsidy campaign, JD.com might not have felt compelled to match discounts. In a less intense competitive climate, its margins would likely have remained closer to historical levels.

adversarial_confounders.impact: Could depress margins independently of competitor subsidies and thus confound the causal link.

details.commentary: PDD's warning about heavy investment and Alibaba's 50 billion yuan subsidy campaign signalled that China's instant commerce players were locked in a costly share grab. As rivals showered consumers and merchants with discounts, JD.com had little choice but to match promotions, deepening the intensity of rivalry and squeezing everyone's margins.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - sluggish demand and subsidy-driven promotion
details.commentary: Sluggish demand and subsidy driven promotion meant the sector relied on price cuts rather than underlying income growth to stimulate spending. In that macro setting, JD.com's push to defend share during a subsidy war exposed it to prolonged margin pressure, which investors increasingly saw as a structural risk.

Rivals' subsidies drew shoppers into their ecosystems, prompting JD.com to respond with its own deals, which then forced competitors to escalate further. This reinforcing loop of ever richer promotions lifted volumes in the short term but steadily diluted profitability, culminating in the sharp margin compression JD.com eventually reported.
